EventStudy: Event Study Analysis in R

Source: R/EventStudy-package.R
EventStudy-package.Rd

Perform financial event study analysis in R. Implements the classical event study methodology (MacKinlay 1997) with multiple return models, parametric and non-parametric test statistics, and visualization tools.

Return Models

  • MarketModel – OLS market model (single factor, optional HAC SEs)

  • MarketAdjustedModel – Market-adjusted returns

  • ComparisonPeriodMeanAdjustedModel – Mean-adjusted returns

  • FamaFrench3FactorModel – Fama-French 3-factor model

  • FamaFrench5FactorModel – Fama-French 5-factor model

  • Carhart4FactorModel – Carhart 4-factor model

  • GARCHModel – GARCH(1,1) model

  • RollingWindowModel – Rolling-window OLS (time-varying beta)

  • DCCGARCHModel – DCC-GARCH (time-varying beta)

  • BHARModel – Buy-and-hold abnormal returns

  • VolumeModel – Volume event study model

  • VolatilityModel – Volatility event study model

Test Statistics

Single-event:

  • ARTTest – Abnormal return t-test

  • CARTTest – Cumulative abnormal return t-test

  • BHARTTest – BHAR t-test

Multi-event:

  • CSectTTest – Cross-sectional t-test

  • PatellZTest – Patell standardized residual test

  • SignTest – Sign test

  • GeneralizedSignTest – Generalized sign test (Cowan 1992)

  • RankTest – Rank test (Corrado 1989)

  • BMPTest – Boehmer, Musumeci & Poulsen (1991) test

  • KolariPynnonenTest – Kolari-Pynnönen adjusted BMP test

  • CalendarTimePortfolioTest – Calendar-time portfolio test

Inference & Robustness

  • adjust_p_values – Multiple testing corrections (BH, Bonferroni, etc.)

  • bootstrap_test – Wild bootstrap inference

  • HAC standard errors via use_hac = TRUE in model constructors

Simulation

  • simulate_event_study – Monte Carlo power analysis

Pipeline

The standard workflow is:

  1. Create an EventStudyTask with data

  2. Define a ParameterSet with model and test choices

  3. Run run_event_study(task, parameter_set) (or the individual steps: prepare_event_study, fit_model, calculate_statistics)

  4. Extract results with get_ar(), get_car(), get_aar(), or tidy.EventStudyTask

  5. Export with export_results

  6. Visualize with plot_event_study

  7. Generate reports with generate_report

Extensions

  • cross_sectional_regression – Explain CARs with firm characteristics

  • IntradayEventStudyTask – Intraday event studies

  • PanelEventStudyTask – Panel DiD event studies (TWFE, Sun-Abraham, Callaway-Sant'Anna, de Chaisemartin-D'Haultfoeuille, Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess)

  • SyntheticControlTask – Synthetic control methods

  • download_stock_data, download_factor_data – Data helpers

References

MacKinlay, A. C. (1997). Event Studies in Economics and Finance. Journal of Economic Literature, 35(1), 13–39.

Fama, E. F. and French, K. R. (1993). Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds. Journal of Financial Economics, 33(1), 3–56.

Carhart, M. M. (1997). On persistence in mutual fund performance. The Journal of Finance, 52(1), 57–82.
